items.title: Exercise 1.7: compact Euclidean LSI-to-PI linearization

source.attribution: Sinho Chewi, Log-Concave Sampling. Original exposition of the compact Euclidean specialization, not a quotation or the full exercise.

items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure, μ a probability measure on E, and C a fixed positive real. Assume the homogeneous function logarithmic Sobolev inequality Entμ(v²) ≤ 2C ∫‖∇v‖² dμ for every compactly supported smooth real v. Then every compactly supported smooth real g has centered second moment ∫(g−∫g dμ)² dμ ≤ C∫‖∇g‖² dμ. No zero-mean condition is imposed on g.
assumptions: One Borel probability measure μ and one fixed C>0 are used throughout. Entμ(q)=∫q log q dμ−(∫q dμ) log(∫q dμ), with 0 log 0=0.
Both compact test classes are C-infinity. Genuine smoothness and the Hilbert gradient are used; a totalized derivative value does not supply smoothness.

No boundedness, zero mean, L², entropy integrability or convergence certificate is added to the observable's premises. The proof constructs these inputs. Finite dimension is used in the cutoff extension.

formulae.label: Compact-test implication
formulae.tex: \forall v\in C_c^\infty(E):\ \operatorname{Ent}_\mu(v^2)\le 2C\int\|\nabla v\|^2\,d\mu\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\forall g\in C_c^\infty(E):\ \int\left(g-\int g\,d\mu\right)^2 d\mu\le C\int\|\nabla g\|^2\,d\mu.

obligations.label: Construct the perturbation and prove compact Poincaré from compact LSI
Wider domain, abstract reversible version and optimal constants remain separate

bindings.boundary: Compact smooth function inequality only. No wider Sobolev/core or abstract Dirichlet-form extension, optimal constant comparison, canonical probability KL/Fisher identification, or complete numbered exercise or QA admission.
